# Draft:China Heritage

China Heritage is a website by Geremie R. Barmé, the Australian sinologist and film-maker on modern and traditional China. The platform is dedicated to exploring various facets of Chinese culture, history, and society, offering in-depth analyses and translations related to China’s heritage.
History
The origins of China Heritage trace back to the China Heritage Quarterly, initially known as the China Heritage Newsletter, which was established in 2005. This e-journal focused on recent developments and scholarship concerning China’s heritage, culture, history, and society. It was produced under the auspices of the China Heritage Project at The Australian National University (ANU). In 2016, Barmé launched China Heritage as a continuation of his commitment to promoting “New Sinology,” providing a platform for scholarly discourse on Chinese cultural and intellectual history.
Content and Focus
China Heritage publishes essays, translations, and analyses that delve into various aspects of Chinese culture and history. The platform addresses contemporary issues within the context of China’s rich cultural heritage, aiming to foster a deeper understanding of the nation’s past and present. Contributions often include discussions on literature, art, politics, and societal changes, reflecting Barmé’s interdisciplinary approach to Sinology.
Editorial Leadership
Geremie R. Barmé, the founder and editor of China Heritage, is a distinguished Australian sinologist, historian, and filmmaker. His academic career includes serving as the founding director of the Australian Centre on China in the World at ANU. Barmé’s work encompasses Chinese cultural and intellectual history from the early modern period to the present, and he has been involved in various scholarly and media projects related to China.
Reception and Impact
China Heritage has been recognized for its scholarly contributions to the field of Chinese studies. The platform’s in-depth articles and translations have been utilized by researchers, students, and individuals interested in Chinese culture and history. Its commitment to providing nuanced perspectives on China’s heritage has solidified its reputation as a valuable resource within the academic community.
